contract_name: ZIPCO Free-plan Event Processing and Resilience Contract
portfolio_claim: Near-real-time bounded event processing with durable recovery and observability; not Kinesis or Firehose streaming.

processing_semantics.invocation: synchronous bounded Lambda batches of 1 to 500 records
processing_semantics.duplicate_policy: transaction_id is the downstream idempotency key
processing_semantics.recovery_point_objective: the complete accepted invocation batch is written to versioned, SSE-KMS S3 raw storage before validation outputs
processing_semantics.recovery_time_objective: operator target under 60 minutes after diagnosis; not load-tested

required_fields.run_id: non-empty string used for lineage and verification

mandatory_controls.assertion: CloudFormation stack status is CREATE_COMPLETE or UPDATE_COMPLETE.
The Lambda event processor state is Active.
The processor uses Python 3.12.
The processor timeout is bounded between 60 and 300 seconds.
The processor enforces event schema version 2.1.0.
Durable event paths use the ZIPCO customer-managed data key.
The processor is isolated to the streaming-free-plan S3 prefix.
Raw S3 contains the complete verification batch.
Curated S3 contains every expected-valid record.
Error S3 contains every expected-invalid record.
Observed raw, curated, and error objects use SSE-KMS.
Curated objects use event-time year/month/day/hour partitions.
The CloudWatch dashboard is retrievable.
Exactly four event-processing metric alarms are deployed.
Exactly one composite health alarm is deployed.
Processor logs have 30-day retention and KMS encryption.
The alert topic uses a rotating customer-managed KMS key.
Processor S3 writes are prefix-scoped and do not use s3:*.
Custom metrics use the ZIPCO/FreePlanEvents namespace.
The publisher passes and replay dry run selects the complete batch.

guardrails: The implementation does not claim Kinesis, Firehose, shard ordering, or native streaming deployment.
Raw data is written before curated and error outputs for every successful invocation.
Replay defaults to dry run, is capped at 500 records, and requires --execute for mutation.
The processor logs aggregate batch metadata only, not full transaction payloads.
This fallback remains separate from the optional paid-plan Firehose reference implementation.
